supersedes: HUMAN_SEAM_REGISTER v1 (14 Aug 2026), which wrongly proposed human takeover of throughput surfaces
design_premise: MarketSquare is AI-first BY DESIGN, not by cost-cutting. AI was chosen for the high-throughput judgement surfaces -- photo triage, moderation, grading, classification, drafting -- because those are exactly where machine speed, consistency and tirelessness beat human judgement. Putting a human on a throughput surface does not make it safer: it throttles the business AND it decays, because a reviewer at high volume rubber-stamps within days. A human seam on a throughput path is a control that LOOKS like a control. Humans are therefore NOT the fallback for AI tasks. Humans own INTERFACES -- the boundaries where MarketSquare meets a party that can compel it: the law, the machine, the partner organisation.

what_catches_a_wrong_answer.note: Bounds, schema, allow-list, idempotency. Cheapest and most reliable. Costs no throughput.

what_catches_a_wrong_answer.mechanism: Second AI lane, different vendor -- DISAGREEMENT is the exception signal
what_catches_a_wrong_answer.note: The +1 provider slot already exists for failover and sits idle in normal operation. On RED surfaces it can double as an adversarial checker: run both lanes, and treat DISAGREEMENT -- not low confidence -- as the exception. Preserves throughput, uses AI's strength to police AI, and turns dormant failover capacity into a live control.
Refund, reserve, or insurance so a wrong answer costs money rather than trust. Money is recoverable; trust is not.
The appeal is itself handled by AI. Only the residue -- the cases the appeal cannot close -- reaches a human interface role.
LAST, and only for exceptions whose CLASS is legal, financial, partner or infrastructural. Never for throughput.

human_roles.owns: What the AI is ALLOWED to say and do. POPIA / consumer law / financial-advice boundary, EULA and disclosure wording, dispute-of-record, counsel and regulator liaison, tax and VAT classification of affiliate income.
human_roles.why_human: The counterparty is a legal system. It requires a named accountable person, signatures, and standing to answer a regulator. No AI can hold that standing.
human_roles.hire_trigger: First regulator or counsel interaction that recurs; or first consumer-law dispute reaching formal stage; or launch in a second jurisdiction.

human_roles.owns: Hetzner host, deploy ref and rollback, backups and restore proofs, SSL, DNS, secret and key custody, breaker Restore after a T3 vendor ban, disk and cost ceilings.
human_roles.why_human: The counterparty is physical and financial infrastructure with irreversible failure modes and credentials that must never sit in an agent's hands. Also the one lane where the maintenance agent cannot be its own safety net.
human_roles.hire_trigger: When David is the single point of failure for a restore -- i.e. before the first period he is unreachable for >24h with live sellers on the platform.

human_roles.owns: Agency contracts and onboarding, Paystack, Travelpayouts, founding-seller relationships, partner escalations, commercial terms.
human_roles.why_human: The counterparty is another human organisation that negotiates, builds trust over time, and will not transact with a bot on terms.
human_roles.hire_trigger: Beyond roughly 5-8 active partner organisations, or the first partner who requires a named account contact in contract.

human_roles.owns: Non-delegable signature: spend above cap, legal sign-off, launch gate, arming autonomy levels, reversing a design ruling.
human_roles.why_human: Accountability cannot be delegated to a system that cannot be held accountable.
human_roles.hire_trigger: Never delegated. Deputised only by formal appointment.

classes.RED: Irreversible harm to a person or to the trust promise. A refund cannot undo it.
classes.AMBER: Money, ranking or reputation. Recoverable, but it costs trust to recover.
classes.GREEN: Cosmetic or retryable. The user retries.

surfaces.decides: Whether an ID document matches the claimed name
surfaces.cost_of_wrong: False accept gives a fraudster a verified badge; false reject locks an honest seller out
surfaces.ai_check: SECOND LANE. Run the +1 vendor on the same document; disagreement routes to appeal. A human reading IDs at volume is slower AND less consistent than either lane.
surfaces.deterministic_guard: Name-match normalisation, document-type allow-list, SSRF-safe fetch (RG-0036)
surfaces.exception_route: AI appeal on reject; unresolved rejects and every false-accept discovered -> R1 Legal
surfaces.trigger: Disagreement rate between lanes >3%, OR any false accept found in production

surfaces.decides: Which copy and photo regions carry identity and must be removed
surfaces.cost_of_wrong: A leaked contact detail destroys the anonymity guarantee and bypasses the intro fee -- the business model itself
surfaces.ai_check: SECOND LANE on the redaction decision plus an adversarial re-read: a separate pass whose only job is to try to RECOVER identity from the anonymised output. If it can, the redaction failed. This is machine-speed red-teaming, impossible for a human at volume.
surfaces.deterministic_guard: Regex sweep for phone/email/URL patterns after AI redaction -- belt and braces, near-zero cost
surfaces.exception_route: Below-threshold held; nothing auto-publishes; contract-level leaks -> R3 Partner, legal exposure -> R1
surfaces.trigger: Adversarial pass recovers identity on any item, OR a leak found in production

surfaces.cost_of_wrong: Unlawful or degrading imagery reaching buyers; or an honest seller silently censored
surfaces.ai_check: SECOND LANE on refusals only (the expensive error is the false accept, so cross-check the accepts on a sampled basis). Refuse rather than blur-to-ruin (RG-0040/0044/0047).
surfaces.deterministic_guard: Judged by bytes not declared type; blur ceiling judges the painted output
surfaces.exception_route: AI appeal on refusal; unlawful-content class -> R1 Legal (reporting duty is a legal act, not a moderation act)
surfaces.trigger: Any reportable-content class detected, OR appeal overturn rate >10%

surfaces.decides: When a user's Tuppence is spent
surfaces.cost_of_wrong: Charging for a service not delivered
surfaces.ai_check: Not an AI decision -- deterministic by design, which is correct
surfaces.deterministic_guard: Charge on delivery only (RG-0033); spend reserved before dispatch (RG-0037); daily ceilings
surfaces.exception_route: Auto-refund on non-delivery (economic absorber); systemic billing faults -> R2, disputes of record -> R1
surfaces.trigger: Refund rate >2% sustained, OR any charge without delivery

surfaces.cost_of_wrong: Buyer receives a card worse than graded; collectables communities punish this permanently
surfaces.ai_check: SECOND LANE above a value threshold; disagreement widens the stated range rather than escalating. AI grades far more consistently than a human grader, who drifts within a single session.
surfaces.deterministic_guard: NOT YET BUILT -- the grade is emitted as fact. Needs 'AI-assisted estimate, not a certified grade' framing plus a value threshold
surfaces.exception_route: Economic absorber: dispute route with refund. Only contract-level disputes -> R1
surfaces.trigger: BUILD NOW: estimate framing + dispute route. Then: dispute rate >1% of graded sales

surfaces.decides: Whether a listed price is fair
surfaces.cost_of_wrong: A confident wrong price anchors a seller low or kills the listing high
surfaces.ai_check: Emit a RANGE from a second lane rather than a single number -- disagreement between lanes IS the honest uncertainty, expressed to the user instead of hidden
surfaces.deterministic_guard: NOT YET BUILT -- sanity bounds against comparable listings on the platform
surfaces.exception_route: None needed; it is advisory by construction once framed as a range
surfaces.trigger: BUILD NOW: range not number, labelled opinion

surfaces.cost_of_wrong: Reads as financial advice -- regulatory exposure well beyond the listing
surfaces.ai_check: Deterministic arithmetic with AI only assembling the inputs. The maths must never be a model output.
surfaces.deterministic_guard: NOT YET BUILT -- computed yield, disclosed formula, disclaimer
surfaces.exception_route: Hand off to partnered agency -- which IS the Tuppence introduction. The exception is the product.
surfaces.trigger: BUILD NOW: disclaimer + agency hand-off. R1 owns the financial-advice boundary wording.

surfaces.cost_of_wrong: A legal notice classified as spam -- the Klarna failure exactly: volume handled, complexity missed
surfaces.ai_check: CLASS-ASYMMETRIC ROUTING: err deliberately toward legal/billing. A false legal flag costs one read; a missed legal notice costs a default judgement. Second lane on anything touching the legal/billing boundary.
surfaces.deterministic_guard: Keyword tripwires (summons, notice, chargeback, regulator, POPIA) force the legal class regardless of model output
surfaces.exception_route: escalation_brief.py renders LEGAL/MONEY/COST/TRUST; legal -> R1, partner -> R3, infra -> R2
surfaces.trigger: HARD RULE: nothing classified legal or billing auto-sends, at any volume

surfaces.decides: The title and description a buyer reads
surfaces.cost_of_wrong: Misdescription is a consumer-law problem once money moves
surfaces.ai_check: The SELLER is the check, and it is the right one -- they alone know the item. Already in the loop.
surfaces.trigger: Only if drafts ever auto-publish. They must not.

surfaces.decides: How a seller raises their trust score
surfaces.cost_of_wrong: Teaches sellers to farm the rubric (see IL-02)
surfaces.ai_check: Not needed -- the risk is in the RUBRIC, not the guidance
surfaces.deterministic_guard: No signal self-reported without evidence; none client-modifiable
surfaces.trigger: Any signal earnable without evidence going live

surfaces.decides: Classifies faults, proposes and ships code patches
surfaces.cost_of_wrong: Highest blast radius in the system -- an autonomous agent shipping to the live site
surfaces.ai_check: Mechanical gates, not a human veto: regression ledger + predeploy + BIT + server auto-rollback. REFUSE_LEGAL_COSTLY / REFUSE_TRUST_CORE force escalation.
surfaces.deterministic_guard: Default OFF; shadow mode; MAX_SHIPS_PER_HOUR; scoped msdeploy SSH user
surfaces.trigger: STANDING CONDITION: any gate that stops asserting re-arms the veto

surfaces.decides: Turns free text into a query
surfaces.cost_of_wrong: Buyer retries; silent failure if it hides a category
surfaces.deterministic_guard: Fallback to keyword search on model failure

surfaces.cost_of_wrong: Bad matches train buyers to ignore notifications permanently
surfaces.ai_check: PARALLEL RUN when the AI matcher replaces the deterministic one -- both run, outputs compared under real load, old lane stays up
surfaces.deterministic_guard: Deterministic keyword matcher is the incumbent
surfaces.trigger: Do not switch off the deterministic lane until the AI lane has beaten it in production

surfaces.cost_of_wrong: Generic advice, ignored -- but it is charged 1T so a bad one costs the seller

incentive_register.test: THE DRAGON TAIL TEST. Dragon Tail never malfunctioned and no missing human would have caught it. Nobody modelled how two independently optimising systems would interact. For every surface where a third party can see platform-internal information: if this actor optimises purely for themselves, what emerges? This is a SYSTEMS-MODELLING question, not a staffing one -- which is why it survives the AI-first design intact.

leaks.if_they_optimise: Enumerate emails, profile spenders, target high-balance sellers
leaks.today: Masked only by the pre-launch edge gate, which LIFTS AT LAUNCH
leaks.action: Authenticate before launch. Launch blocker. Owner: R2.

leaks.surface: Trust rubric fully published; Gold 90+ earns featured priority
leaks.if_they_optimise: Farm the cheapest points to 90 without becoming more trustworthy; referrals (evidence_required varies) are the vector
leaks.action: Referrals need evidence before the lane goes live. Owner: R4.

leaks.surface: Boost lowers the match threshold 60 -> 45 and sorts boosted-first
leaks.if_they_optimise: Boost weak listings to reach buyers they should not; buyers learn boosted results are worse and stop trusting the feed
leaks.action: Boost raises VISIBILITY, never lowers RELEVANCE. Decouple. Owner: R4.

leaks.surface: Intro costs the seller 1T, 2T if boosted -- pay to be reachable
leaks.if_they_optimise: Sellers suppress boost to pay less and become less reachable; gated buyers route around the platform
leaks.today: LM-T1 idempotency, LM-15 trust gate, LM-F3 cooldown
leaks.action: Any incentive making a seller LESS reachable works against the only thing the till charges for. Owner: R4.

leaks.surface: Anonymisation is all that stands between an agency and a free bypass of the intro fee
leaks.if_they_optimise: Probe the anonymiser for the copy pattern that survives it
leaks.action: Adversarial AI re-read (AS-02) is the right control -- machine-speed red-teaming, continuous. Owner: R3.

leaks.surface: super_example exemplars pinned first in every sort
leaks.if_they_optimise: Conclude the platform favours its own demos and disengage
leaks.action: Holding. Re-check when real listing volume passes demo volume. Owner: R4.

predesign_rules.detail: No mechanism is replaced without both running side by side and compared under real load. The parallel lane is AI-versus-AI or AI-versus-deterministic -- never AI-versus-human, which cannot keep pace and so proves nothing.

predesign_rules.rule: AI IS POLICED BY AI; HUMANS OWN INTERFACES
predesign_rules.detail: A wrong AI answer is caught by a deterministic guard, a second vendor lane, or an economic absorber. Humans are not the fallback for AI tasks -- they own the boundaries where MarketSquare meets the law (R1), the machine (R2), a partner organisation (R3), or must sign (R4).

predesign_rules.rule: NEVER REMOVE THE FALLBACK AND ADD THE NEW LANE IN THE SAME CHANGE
predesign_rules.detail: Yum mandated Dragon Tail AND centralised the DoorDash contract at once, so the franchise lost the AI's replacement and its own tools simultaneously. One change at a time.

predesign_rules.rule: RUN THE DRAGON TAIL TEST ON EVERY NEW INFORMATION SURFACE
predesign_rules.detail: Before exposing any platform-internal signal to sellers, buyers, agencies or affiliates, write down what a purely self-interested actor does with it. Systems modelling, not staffing.

predesign_rules.rule: NO PUBLIC CLAIM THE MACHINERY CANNOT YET HONOUR
predesign_rules.detail: Klarna's most expensive loss was narrative. Extend the vendor-neutral copy discipline (RG-0035) to capability claims.

predesign_rules.rule: A HUMAN IN A THROUGHPUT PATH IS A DEFECT, NOT A CONTROL
predesign_rules.detail: It throttles the business and it decays -- a reviewer at volume rubber-stamps within days, leaving a control that only looks like one. If a design puts a human on a per-item path, the design is wrong. human_seam_check.py fails it.

predesign_rules.rule: THE EXCEPTION RATE IS THE TRIGGER, NEVER THE VOLUME
predesign_rules.detail: A human interface role engages when the exception RATE crosses a threshold, or when the exception CLASS is legal, financial, partner or infrastructural. Rising volume is the design working, and must never pull a human in.

predesign_rules.rule: THE +1 LANE IS A CONTROL, NOT JUST A SPARE
predesign_rules.detail: The designated swap-out provider sits idle in normal operation. On RED surfaces, run it as a second opinion and treat DISAGREEMENT -- not low confidence -- as the exception signal. Dormant failover capacity becomes a live, throughput-preserving control.

predesign_rules.rule: EVERY RED SURFACE RUNS DO -> CHECK, AND THE CHECKER IS CHECKED
predesign_rules.detail: The doer produces, an independent cheaper checker inspects the artefact against a written spec, and seeded defects prove the checker can still see. QC gates the item; QA audits the system -- MarketSquare had QA and no QC, and QA cannot catch an individual bad answer because it never looks at individual answers.

qc_pipeline.pattern: DO -> CHECK, serial, in-line, per item
qc_pipeline.qc_not_qa: QA audits the PROCESS -- periodic, sampled, preventive. MarketSquare already had it: regression_ledger.py, audit_global_qa.py, BIT, the golden-set eval. QC inspects the PRODUCT -- per item, in-line, detective. MarketSquare had NONE. QA cannot gate an item because it does not look at items, which is why adding more QA never catches the individual bad answer. The doer is the engineer; the checker is the inspector, and they must not be the same mind.

constraints.failure_prevented: A checker without written acceptance criteria re-does the task with an opinion and its verdicts drift. QCSpec is mandatory; criteria phrased as taste ('well written', 'appropriate') are refused at validate().

constraints.rule: The checker never sees the doer's reasoning
constraints.failure_prevented: Shown a rationale, the checker grades the argument instead of the artefact and a confident explanation buys a pass. The harness builds the checker prompt from (input, spec, artefact) only -- there is no parameter through which reasoning could arrive.

constraints.rule: Different lane by default; correlation declared, never hidden
constraints.failure_prevented: A model checking its own output tends to ratify it, and same-family models share blind spots. Checker binds cross-vendor; with one lane configured the verdict is stamped independence='correlated' rather than pretending to independence it does not have.

constraints.rule: The checker is cheaper than the doer, not bigger
constraints.failure_prevented: Judging against explicit criteria is easier than generating. A heavyweight checker doubles cost and latency for no gain and makes the chain the bottleneck -- the classic serial-pipeline death, and the exact throughput objection that rules humans out.
DO -> CHECK -> REDO with no cap burns money and may never converge. max_attempts enforced; exhaustion sets escalate=True and routes to the owning interface role.

constraints.rule: The checker is itself checked -- seeded defects
constraints.failure_prevented: A checker that passes everything looks perfect and is blind. Every spec carries canaries -- known-bad artefacts it MUST reject, on the specific criterion they violate. This is the known-defect sample from an industrial inspection line, and the only honest answer to 'who checks the checker'.
Every verdict records doer lane/model, checker lane/model, spec id@version, attempt and failed criteria, so a bad batch can be traced and recalled rather than guessed at.
An unavailable checker, unparseable JSON, or a citation of criteria that do not exist all return passed=False with escalate=True. A checker that cannot speak is never a pass.

candidates.doer: redact identity from agency copy and photos
candidates.checker: ADVERSARIAL -- try to RECOVER identity from the redacted output; success means the redaction failed
candidates.why_first: Highest value, lowest risk, defends the intro fee which is the entire till. The adversarial form is strictly stronger than criteria-matching, and only a machine can run it on every item.

candidates.checker: no contact details, no real business named (SO-1), required fields present, claims match the photos
candidates.why_first: Highest volume, consumer-law exposure once money moves, and the criteria are cleanly objective.

candidates.checker: sampled cross-check of ACCEPTS (the false accept is the expensive error, and an accept is never appealed by anyone)
candidates.why_first: RED and high throughput. Rejects get appealed and self-correct; accepts are silent, so the checker must look where nobody complains.

candidates.checker: document integrity, name-match logic, no extraction the image cannot support
candidates.why_first: RED, and the false-accept is the expensive error.

candidates.checker: is the grade supported by visible evidence in the photos, and is the estimate framing present
candidates.why_first: Clears an AMBER warn and defuses the collectables reputational risk.

candidates.doer: classify inbound mail and draft a reply
candidates.checker: legal/billing boundary only -- was anything with legal or money characteristics classified away from it
candidates.why_first: Narrow, cheap, and it is precisely the Klarna failure mode.
